title: AQA GCSE Biology · Variation, Evolution and Classification

items.stem: Which of these describes the causes of variation between individuals in a population?

options.text: Inherited genes, the conditions of development, or both
Inherited genes alone, which are passed on by the parents
Mutations that are produced by a change in the environment
Mutations alone, because every one changes the phenotype

items.why: Variation may be due to the genes they have inherited, the conditions in which they have developed, or a combination of genes and the environment.

items.stem: All variants arise from mutations. Which statement about mutations and phenotype is correct?

options.text: Most mutations lead to a change in the phenotype
Most mutations have no effect on the phenotype
Mutations happen only when the environment changes
Mutations build up in an organism during its life

items.why: Most variants have no effect on the phenotype, some influence phenotype and very few determine phenotype.

items.stem: Which statement describes evolution?

options.text: A change in the characteristics of an animal in its lifetime
A change in the inherited characteristics of a population
A change in appearance that makes a population a new species
The growth of the characteristics that organisms need most

items.why: Evolution is a change in the inherited characteristics of a population over time through a process of natural selection.

items.stem: Which statement about selective breeding is correct?

options.text: It removes inherited defects from the breeds produced
It happens in wild populations with no human choice
It can lead to inbreeding in the breeds it produces
It adds a gene from another organism to the offspring

items.why: Selective breeding can lead to 'inbreeding' where some breeds are particularly prone to disease or inherited defects.

items.stem: What happens in genetic engineering?

options.text: A gene is transferred to the cells of another organism
Parents with the desired characteristic are bred together
Cells from one organism are grown into identical copies
A faulty gene in a patient is replaced to cure a disorder

items.why: Genes from the chromosomes of humans and other organisms can be 'cut out' and transferred to cells of other organisms, modifying the genome.

items.stem: Which statement about the uses of genetic engineering is correct?

options.text: Bacterial cells have been engineered to make human insulin
Tissue culture is used to insert genes in bacterial cells
Inherited disorders are now cured using genetic modification
Crops are engineered by breeding the best plants together

items.why: Bacterial cells have been genetically engineered to produce useful substances such as human insulin to treat diabetes.

items.stem: Which statement describes the main steps in the process of genetic engineering?

options.text: Enzymes isolate the gene, which a vector puts into cells
Enzymes cut out the gene and carry it into the cells
Cells are taken from an organism and grown into copies
The best parent organisms are bred to combine genes

items.why: Enzymes are used to isolate the required gene, this gene is inserted into a vector, usually a bacterial plasmid or a virus, and the vector is used to insert the gene into the required cells at an early stage of their development.

items.stem: Two plants grown from cuttings of the same parent plant are given different amounts of light. One grows much taller than the other. What does this difference show?

options.text: The plants inherited different genes for their height
The change in light has caused a mutation in one plant
The environment has influenced the phenotype of the plants
One plant has evolved to be taller in the brighter light

items.why: The genome and its interaction with the environment influence the development of the phenotype, so the different light conditions have produced different heights.

items.stem: A mutation produces a new phenotype in a population. The environment then changes, and the new phenotype is suited to the new conditions. What is the likely result?

options.text: More mutations of the same type occur in the population
A relatively rapid change in the species can take place
Each organism changes to the new phenotype in its lifetime
The organisms develop the new phenotype that they need

items.why: If the new phenotype is suited to an environmental change it can lead to a relatively rapid change in the species.

items.stem: Two populations of one species have been separated for a very long time and now look very different. What must be shown before they are classed as two new species?

options.text: That their phenotypes are different enough to tell apart
That each population has developed the features that it needs
That the individuals have changed during their own lifetimes
That they can no longer produce fertile offspring together

items.why: Two new species have formed when the populations are so different in phenotype that they can no longer interbreed to produce fertile offspring.

items.stem: A nursery needs many new plants that are identical to one rare parent plant. Which statement is correct?

options.text: A gene from another plant would give identical copies
Tissue culture of the parent's cells gives identical plants
Cuttings from the parent give plants showing variation
One generation of breeding would give identical offspring

items.why: Tissue culture uses small groups of cells from part of a plant to grow identical new plants, which is important for preserving rare plant species.

items.stem: In adult cell cloning the nucleus is removed from an unfertilised egg cell, the nucleus from an adult skin cell is inserted, and an electric shock makes the egg cell divide to form an embryo. What are the embryo cells like?

options.text: They have the genetic information of the egg donor
They have genetic information varying from the adult
They have an extra gene added from another organism
They have the same genetic information as the skin cell

items.why: These embryo cells contain the same genetic information as the adult skin cell whose nucleus was inserted into the egg cell.

items.stem: In a beetle population most beetles are pale and a few are dark. The tree bark the beetles live on becomes darker, so birds find the pale beetles more easily. After many generations most of the beetles are dark. Which statement explains this?

options.text: The beetles developed a dark colour because they needed it
Each pale beetle became darker as the tree bark got darker
The darker bark caused the mutations that made beetles darker
Dark beetles survived to breed and passed on their variant

items.why: Natural selection acts on variants that give rise to phenotypes best suited to their environment, and those beetles pass the genes on to the next generation.

items.stem: A farmer chooses the cows that produce the most milk and breeds them together. From their offspring he again breeds those that produce the most milk, and he repeats this for many generations. Which statement about this process is correct?

options.text: It is natural selection, as the best cows survive and breed
It is genetic engineering, as the genome is being modified
It is selective breeding, as the farmer chose the parents
It was complete once the first chosen cows had been bred

items.why: Selective breeding is the process by which humans breed animals for particular genetic characteristics, here the useful characteristic of producing more milk.

items.stem: Which statement about genetically modified (GM) crops is correct?

options.text: GM crops generally produce lower yields than other food crops
GM crops are grown from cells taken from one parent plant
GM crops may affect populations of wild flowers and insects
GM crops are used to cure inherited disorders in patients

items.why: Concerns about GM crops include the effect on populations of wild flowers and insects, and some people feel the effects on human health have not been fully explored.

items.stem: Which of these is a reason why the theory of evolution by natural selection was only gradually accepted?

options.text: Scientists in 1859 were at once convinced by the evidence.
The mechanism of inheritance was not known for 50 more years.
Lamarck had shown that changes made in life are inherited.
Darwin had already explained inheritance in terms of genes.

items.why: The mechanism of inheritance and variation was not known until 50 years after the theory was published, which is one of the reasons given for the theory being only gradually accepted.

items.stem: What was Alfred Russel Wallace's contribution to the theory of evolution by natural selection?

options.text: He collected specimens overseas for Darwin's new book.
He explained natural selection using genes and DNA.
He proposed the same theory independently of Darwin.
He convinced other scientists to accept the theory.

items.why: Alfred Russel Wallace independently proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection and published joint writings with Darwin in 1858, which prompted Darwin to publish On the Origin of Species the following year.

items.stem: Which statement about the theory of speciation is correct?

options.text: More evidence has changed our understanding over time.
Wallace gathered the evidence for Darwin's own ideas.
Two groups are new species once they look different.
Wallace's ideas on speciation were accepted at once.

items.why: Alfred Wallace did much pioneering work on speciation but more evidence over time has led to our current understanding of the theory of speciation.

items.stem: What did Mendel conclude from his breeding experiments on plants?

options.text: That genes made of DNA are carried on the chromosomes.
That the environment creates a plant's characteristics.
That plant breeding could not explain inheritance.
That 'units' pass on each characteristic unchanged.

items.why: One of Mendel's observations was that the inheritance of each characteristic is determined by 'units' that are passed on to descendants unchanged.

items.stem: What happened in the mid-20th Century in the development of gene theory?

options.text: Mendel described the first genes made of DNA in plants.
Darwin's theory explained inheritance by using genes.
Mendel's 'units' were proved wrong by chromosome work.
The structure of DNA and gene function were worked out.

items.why: In the mid-20th Century the structure of DNA was determined and the mechanism of gene function worked out. This scientific work by many scientists led to the gene theory being developed.

items.stem: In a beetle population, shell thickness varies. Predators cannot eat the thickest-shelled beetles. After many generations most beetles have thick shells. Why?

options.text: Beetles grew thicker shells in life and passed them on.
Thick-shelled beetles survived to breed and passed this on.
Beetles needed thicker shells, so they grew them to survive.
Predators made thick shells appear in the beetle population.

items.why: Individuals with characteristics most suited to the environment are more likely to survive to breed successfully, and the characteristics that have enabled these individuals to survive are then passed on to the next generation.

items.stem: Giraffes with longer necks can reach more leaves. How would a biologist today explain why giraffes now have long necks?

options.text: Reaching high leaves created the long neck characteristic.
Necks stretched during life were passed to the offspring.
Giraffes needed longer necks, so their necks became longer.
Giraffes with longer necks survived and bred more often.

items.why: Individuals with characteristics most suited to the environment are more likely to survive to breed successfully, and those characteristics are then passed on to the next generation.

items.stem: Two populations of one snail species are separated by a new river. What must finally happen for them to become two different species?

options.text: They must look different enough to be told apart by eye.
They must change during life and pass these changes on.
They must not be able to breed to give fertile young.
The river must create new characteristics in each group.

items.why: The isolated populations experience different conditions, so natural selection selects different characteristics in each. Over many generations they become so different that they can no longer interbreed to produce fertile offspring, and they are then two species.

items.stem: Which statement about the development of our understanding of genetics is correct?

options.text: Darwin used genes to explain variation when he published.
Chromosome behaviour was observed after Mendel's work.
Mendel discovered DNA during his experiments on plants.
Mendel's 'units' were rejected once chromosomes were seen.

items.why: Mendel carried out his breeding experiments in the mid-19th Century; in the late 19th Century behaviour of chromosomes during cell division was observed, and in the early 20th Century it was observed that chromosomes and Mendel's 'units' behaved in similar ways, leading to the idea that the 'units', now called genes, were located on chromosomes.

items.stem: Which observation is evidence that supports the theory of evolution by natural selection?

options.text: Antibiotic resistance evolves in bacterial populations.
Dead organisms are turned into fossils in the rocks.
Animals that exercise pass strength to their young.
The fossil record gives us a complete history of life.

items.why: Evidence for Darwin's theory is now available in the fossil record and in the knowledge of how resistance to antibiotics evolves in bacteria, and it has been shown that characteristics are passed on to offspring in genes. The theory is now widely accepted.

items.stem: Which statement about how fossils are formed is correct?

options.text: Bones and shells are kept, but footprints are not.
A dead organism will turn into a fossil in the rock.
Traces such as footprints and burrows are preserved.
The fossil record includes each species from the past.

items.why: Fossils may be formed as preserved traces of organisms, such as footprints, burrows and rootlet traces, as well as from undecayed parts and from parts replaced by minerals as they decay.

items.stem: A species of bird disappears from Earth after a volcanic eruption destroys its habitat. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The species is extinct once its numbers fall very low.
Human hunting is what makes a species become extinct.
Fossils show the exact date each species died out.
A catastrophic event can cause a species to die out.

items.why: Extinctions occur when there are no remaining individuals of a species still alive, and a single catastrophic event such as a massive volcanic eruption is one of the factors which may contribute to extinction.

items.stem: Which action would reduce the rate of development of antibiotic resistant strains?

options.text: Prescribing antibiotics to treat viral infections.
Restricting the use of antibiotics in agriculture.
Stopping a course of antibiotics when symptoms go.
Relying on new antibiotics being developed quickly.

items.why: The agricultural use of antibiotics should be restricted, which is one of the measures given for reducing the rate of development of antibiotic resistant strains.

items.stem: Why was the importance of Mendel's discovery not recognised until after his death?

options.text: His breeding results were later shown to be incorrect.
He had described genes before DNA had been discovered.
His work was accepted by other scientists straight away.
The behaviour of chromosomes had not yet been seen.

items.why: Mendel worked in the mid-19th Century. Behaviour of chromosomes during cell division was only observed in the late 19th Century, and only in the early 20th Century was it observed that chromosomes and Mendel's 'units' behaved in similar ways.

items.stem: Why can scientists not be certain about how life began on Earth?

options.text: Scientists have now collected the earliest fossils.
Early organisms had bones which dissolved in rocks.
Early life was soft-bodied and left few traces behind.
Early organisms became fossils that we can study.

items.why: Many early forms of life were soft-bodied, which means that they have left few traces behind, and what traces there were have been mainly destroyed by geological activity.

items.stem: An evolutionary tree shows species P and Q meeting at a branch point, with species R branching off much earlier. What does the tree show?

options.text: P and Q share a more recent common ancestor than R.
Species Q evolved directly from species P over time.
P and Q are separate species as they look different.
The tree shows each of the species that has lived.

items.why: A branch point on an evolutionary tree represents an ancestor shared by the organisms above it, so the later the branch point, the more recently the organisms shared an ancestor and the less they have changed from each other.

items.stem: A patient's MRSA infection is not killed by an antibiotic. Why has the population of the resistant strain risen?

options.text: Resistant bacteria survived and reproduced rapidly.
The antibiotic changed the bacteria so they resist it.
The bacteria needed to resist, so they became resistant.
Each bacterium became resistant and passed this on.

items.why: Some strains produced by mutation might be resistant to antibiotics, and so are not killed. They survive and reproduce, so the population of the resistant strain rises, and bacteria can evolve rapidly because they reproduce at a fast rate.

items.stem: In the three-domain system developed by Carl Woese, into which three groups are organisms divided?

options.text: Archaea, Bacteria and Eukaryota
Bacteria, Protists and Eukaryota
Archaea, Bacteria and Protists
Archaea, Bacteria and Animals

items.why: Due to evidence available from chemical analysis, organisms are divided into Archaea, Bacteria and Eukaryota, with protists, fungi, plants and animals included in Eukaryota.

items.stem: A student is given the names of two organisms: Panthera leo and Panthera pardus. Which Linnaean group is given by the shared name Panthera?

options.text: Their order in the Linnaean system
Their family in the Linnaean system
Their genus in the Linnaean system
Their species in the Linnaean system

items.why: Organisms are named by the binomial system of genus and species, so the first part of each name, Panthera, gives the genus that the two organisms share.

items.stem: Linnaeus classified living things depending on their structure and characteristics. Why were new models of classification later proposed?

options.text: Because much larger numbers of species were discovered
Because improved microscopes showed internal structures
Because fossils of many extinct organisms were discovered
Because bacteria were found in many extreme environments

items.why: As evidence of internal structures became more developed due to improvements in microscopes, and the understanding of biochemical processes progressed, new models of classification were proposed.
